title: Can I get some feedback on my game?
author: TheKaleKing
selftext:
[https://flight747.vercel.app/](https://flight747.vercel.app/)  
  
So I'm almost done with my game so now I'm trying to get some feedback on it, and I don't have that many friends to share it with so that would be great if some of you can test it for just a few minutes, playing just 1 minute you get the feel of what it is, even then the boss spawns at 2 mins! ;)  
  
It's a mix of endless runner, and roguelike and planes which is a really weird mix honestly but I was doing this project as a test and I'm proud of the result. I really love planes, and last year I really got hooked into megabonk, and then I wanted something fairly simple for mobile so I went with the endlress runner idea and combined all 3 together.  
  
I honestly think there might be too much "stuff" in the screen, it's a bit chaotic but also kinda fun. Let me know what you think. No hurt feelings, feel free to roast it if you need to, just trying to get it a little bit better before I put it on the google play store (free android app).  


As for my workflow, it's a Phaser game that I made in typescript. Usually I do Unity BUT I wanted to try for this project with some typescript because I notice AI is super good with react apps so wanted to see if there would be a big difference with TS versus C#, and it's hard to tell honestly BUT the main thing that I really enjoyed was the no compile time, that has been huge compared to Unity waiting 20-30 seconds everytime you change a line of code. Making changes for this project, tweaking a few things here and there has been much easier than unity so I really enjoyed it. Phaser seems fine, wasn't really hard to understand the code so I don't have really strong opinions on that.

For the code I used claude code for the whole project, and for the images it's a mix of ChatGPT/Grok/Gemini, [suno.ai](http://suno.ai) for music, and elevenlabs for sound effects.

Let me know if you have other questions about the workflow or feedback/suggestions for the game.

Thank you!

[https://flight747.vercel.app/](https://flight747.vercel.app/)

comments.author: IAmhowlshot
comments.body: I like planes, i love the variety of them haha. Runs well, good visuals. The idea of crashing your planes into others is weird for regular passenger planes though lol. I like the variety of choosing upgrades on level up too, and maybe the extra planes you unlock that fight for you can be spaced away from the main, but overall it is interesting and looks decent

replies.author: TheKaleKing

replies.author: Ok_Try_877
replies.body: Also my first upgrade was a Concorde plane that shot.... I would associate Concorde with speed.... not combat, being as its a passenger plane. I also was a little confused with the crashing into planes to get bonuses... on a game where the idea is not to get hit by stuff.... Id make the planes and everything stuff you dodge unless its very clearly a flashing powerup or chest... so you not trying to understand what you should be crashing into and what you should be dodging... Also its a bit werid to get a bonus for crashing in a dodging game...

In the beginning yes since it's the tutorial, it explains that you need to dodge the bird poop but it doesn't damage you if you don't, since it's just the tutorial.

If that happened past the beginning, though that's not normal and you found a bug haha. Thanks for trying it out! :)

replies.author: TheKaleKing

comments.author: Mikedzines
comments.body:
**Some thoughts:**

\- The graphics are really bright and polished.  
\- The gameplay is easy to pick up and the potato-bro style mechanics add variety to the game

How i would optimize.. zoom out / scale the entire game back by 50%

I think the tutorial is SUPER easy-- almost to point where it makes the game NOT fun.. but after that, around level 3, it ramps up in difficulty to the point where there are a lot of things of inconsistent size flying at screen.

Try to group them like t-shirt sizes that increase variety over many levels.. its happening too fast at the moment.

replies.author: TheKaleKing
replies.body:
Thank you for the feedback much appreciated. I will try making the tutorial a bit more fun, scale down early difficulty and also zoom out the game to see how it feels.

What do you mean group them like t-shirt sizes? Do you mean only spawning a specific things after a certain level so there's not too much at the start or something else?

Much appreciated!

replies.author: Mikedzines
replies.body:
Yes! exactly.

T-shirts are small, medium, large.. but you also have extra small and extra large.  
Treat your projectile sprites like that.

Drip-feed complexity out to the player and it will feel more challenging.   
You can even use AI to figure out the difficulty curve on that by analyzing other games!

replies.author: TheKaleKing
replies.body:
Done :) It now starts with seagulls until level 4 and then another enemy and then until level 8 where you unlock all 3 it's much smoother. Thank you!

I tried the zoom out thing too but I didn't really like it so I kept it as is for that one but it was worth a try.

replies.author: TheKaleKing

comments.author: LogDoubtDev
comments.body: Pretty fun spin on a Vampire Survivors style game roguelite.  As others have said, crashing into other planes feels unintuitive, especially when you have a mix of enemies and planes.  You might consider reworking the experience system.  Maybe some crates on parachutes falling downward, I think that would also help differentiate from enemies.

replies.author: TheKaleKing
replies.body:
Thank you! That's a fair point that you bring up there on it being not intuitive crashing into other planes. The basic idea was that planes can never hurt you like everything plane is cool so only other stuff can hurt you.

I think I love planes too much so that somehow made sense in my head? haha

I might change it at some point but my goal is to send the game on the app store this weekend so tweaking a few more things but I kinda like crashing into other planes it gets kinda fun.

The crates on a parachute thing sounds really fun though I could add that.

Thanks for the feedback, much appreciated, and thank you for trying out the game!

Sounds like you have a lot of actual experience though, while I’m just a noob trying to vibecode :p. Congrats, fun idea and runs great!!

replies.author: LAWsyndrome
replies.body: One impression was the only thing that felt threatening were the crows, everything else, after enough upgrades was just “sort of try to dodge”

replies.author: TheKaleKing
replies.body:
Fair point indeed when you're strong enough seagulls are just free xp basically. I wanted to put as much "stuff" in the screen to blow up so that's kinda their purpose so to speak once you're strong enough but maybe the pigeons should get tankier so you don't blow them one shot and you actually have to dodge their bullet that would hurt the more the game goes because you are right you're blowing everything except the crows that you have to dodge.

Much appreciated and keep on grinding!

replies.author: TheKaleKing
replies.body: Thank you for the kind words I appreciate it. I am indeed a software eng as a job but never let that discourage you. We're in the best time right now to LEARN how to code. You can use AI to teach you coding principles so that you can understand how to vibe code better and doing it on a project that you're actually having fun doing. Keep grinding. Try claude code if you haven't it's a game changer.

For the chests, I could add the stats that they give and make them rarer I might play around with that too.

replies.author: makkoaigames
replies.body:
The boss was definitely too easy until he was not. I’d advocate for adding a couple of movesets/attacks to the boss so you can build random patterns to keep the challenge interesting without it going from “I just killed this thing in one shot” to “I got nicked by a bone and died”

I’d change the damage on the bones to a range (it might already be this way), and then reuse seagull and poop waves randomly to mix it up.

replies.author: TheKaleKing
replies.body:
Good idea. It's a constant damage I think so I can definitely change that. I agree I could see if I could add a few more movesets without making it too confusing. If I could add 2 more maybe that would be enough. Let me know if you have ideas.

on top of my head I'm thinking like that the boss actually tries to ram you instead of throwing something as an additional one.
